key_insight: ArchSpace centers on making LLM architecture research easier to record, review, and reference. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so specific mechanisms and demonstrated findings cannot be confirmed.
problem_solved: Architecture research is difficult to compare and build upon: industry reports rarely explain abandoned ideas or design decisions, while academic studies often rely on limited compute, inconsistent baselines, and small-scale evaluations.
method: Record architectural ideas and experimental outcomes to make research decisions more transparent.
Review architecture evidence with attention to evaluation scale and baseline consistency.
Support referencing prior architecture research; these high-level aims are inferred from the title, not verified implementation details.
impact: More transparent, comparable architecture evidence could help practitioners choose designs and avoid repeating unsuccessful experiments. This matters because architecture affects scaling behavior, training efficiency, and inference cost.
visual_elements: Industry–academia comparison: missing decision histories versus limited compute and inconsistent baselines.

paper_title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
paper_authors: Jie Wang, Tong Zhu, JiaHao Kuang, Zhe Xu, Yunkai Chai
